pillar_reactions.evidence: After the full training and mobility pitch the reaction was flat but positive: 'So far sounds good. I mean, working less days and less time sounds good.' The less-time framing was the part that landed - he had complained about 1.5-2 hour sessions.
The rep pre-framed his nutrition as already good and pitched only tweaks to the eating window; the entire response was 'Yeah.' at 00:40:27. No questions, no pushback, no engagement.

Asked twice about mechanics. First: 'If I'm doing this program full and we're doing three to four times a week, am I supposed to just, like, be not doing any workouts at the gym anymore?' Then: 'How are the workouts done? Is it like a good through a Zoom call, or is it just watching videos, or just doing things on your own at home or at the gym?' He also pushed for the breakdown at price - 'what's the breakdown of that over six months, in terms of, like, days per week or meetings and one-on-ones?' - and got a vague answer.

anchors.raw: if I'm going to work with anybody, it has to be something that like, can't just either do myself at the gym or find on YouTube and kind of, you know, it's not, it's not for a lack of, uh, or lack of desire. I often try to throw money at a problem. Whereas if I could just do my own research and take the initiative to do it, I could figure it out.
anchors.note: He had already been running Trevor's free YouTube content for a month and getting results from it - 'I've seen Trevor's stuff online, so he and a few other people that I found on YouTube, I'll start to do some of the exercises'. The free version of the product is his baseline, so $6,000 has to beat something he is already doing for nothing.

anchors.raw: I'm actually, I'm investigating a couple of other opportunities right now. So I have to, you know, I have to meet with this trainer. I've got another person from the internet that I'm meeting with this week also.
anchors.competitor: an unnamed trainer at his gym and an unnamed online coach
anchors.note: Neither was priced on the call, so the anchor is unquantified, but it is live - both meetings are inside the same week and he called this 'the first person I'm speaking to about this on a serious level'. Being first in a three-way comparison at $6,000 with no urgency mechanism is a weak position.

anchors.raw: I go, if I see, I see a chiropractor, like, one, once or twice a week, and I'm, I just, I with a physical therapist recently who I might start seeing.
anchors.note: He is already paying weekly or twice-weekly for physical care and about to add a PT, which establishes both willingness to spend on his body and monthly outflow already committed. The rep did not quantify or use it.

anchors.raw: I'm supposed to, I'm supposed to meet up with a new trainer potentially at my gym, but I, I have to talk to her and see what she's, you know, offering. Cause I don't know, I don't know if she's just sort of a typical, you know, let's just do one machine at a time kind of person, which is not what I'm looking for.
anchors.note: Gym PT rates are the implicit reference point for what coaching costs. The rep dismissed it in one line - 'it doesn't sound like that is something you want to do' - rather than pricing the comparison out loud, so the anchor was never displaced.

unmet_demand.want: Programming that is genuinely built around an actively painful right shoulder that cannot tolerate overhead loading, an L4/L5 herniation and post-autoimmune recovery capacity - the thing every previous trainer got wrong.
unmet_demand.why_unmet: The offer's answer was volume and load management ('we want to make sure the shoulders are going to be handled more lightly'), delivered by asynchronous video form review. There is no clinical screening step, no clearance requirement and no clinician in the delivery model, and the rep did not offer to coordinate with the PT or chiropractor who are already treating the shoulder. Whether a kettlebell programme built on swings, cleans and overhead pressing can be safely regressed this far was asserted, never validated.

unmet_demand.want: A concrete breakdown of contact time - how many one-on-one sessions, how often, over six months - before deciding on $6,000.
unmet_demand.why_unmet: He asked directly and the answer was 'he jumps on whenever it's needed. So it's not like a specific every week, every month or anything.' The programme almost certainly has a defined delivery cadence (onboarding call, daily video feedback, weekly check-ins, Thursday live workouts) and those elements had all been described earlier, but at the moment of price they were not restated as a countable deliverable.
